lead: Taylor's self-titled debut is turning 20, and her official site has given it a room of its own. Fans found the new archive section in late October, just as the album's long-promised rerecording is still waiting on a release date.

sentences.text: Fans noticed a new "20 years of Taylor Swift" section on taylorswift.com on October 23, Yahoo says.
It gathers streaming links, photos, career highlights and the earliest music videos in one place.
Taylor Nation marked the anniversary with an Instagram clip that runs through every one of her eras.
Taylor herself stayed quiet on social media for the day.
That quiet keeps one question alive, because the debut is the one record whose new version fans still haven't heard.
In her letter about buying back her first six masters, Taylor said she had already rerecorded the whole album, Elle notes.
No release of that version has been announced.
The anniversary also brings back the story of a door that almost opened differently: Richard Marx turned down a co-write with a 15-year-old Taylor after Scott Borchetta played him her first demos.
Two decades later, he still says he wouldn't have been any good to her.

lead: After three weeks on top, "Patient Zero" has stepped down from the Hot 100 summit, and the reason is more about the record shelf than the radio. The song now sits inside a top five packed with fresh debuts.

sentences.text: "Patient Zero" slipped from No. 1 to No. 5 this week, ending a three-week run at the top, Rolling Stone reports.
Physical sales fell from 151,000 to 26,000, with no new variants or shipments to keep them up, Variety says.
The acoustic versions still added 4,000 downloads to the week.
Ella Langley's "Choosin' Texas" is back at No. 1 for a 25th nonconsecutive week.
Tate McRae's "Housewife" debuted right behind it at No. 2 on 22.9 million streams.
The dip follows a historic start: the song debuted at No. 1 as Taylor's 16th chart-topper and her 10th to enter at the summit, tying Drake's record.
It also spent three straight weeks at No. 1 in the UK while "The Life of a Showgirl" reached 15 weeks atop the Billboard 200.

lead: A Chiefs game day used to come with a Taylor sighting almost by default, but November 1 looked different. While Kansas City played in Denver, she appears to have spent the day at a Toy Story 5 screening instead.

sentences.text: MARCA's game-day preview asked whether Taylor would be at the Chiefs-Broncos game and said nothing had been confirmed.
She had been at Arrowhead for the teams' Week 1 meeting.
US Magazine reports she did not appear to be at the game, in line with a recent pattern of skipping road trips with Travis and the team.
She appears to have spent the day at a For Your Consideration screening of Toy Story 5.
Home games are a different story: she was in the Arrowhead suite with Caitlin Clark and Este Haim for the 22-6 win over the Chargers.
The film she chose over the road trip is having a moment of its own, with "I Knew It, I Knew You" now up for a Hollywood Music in Media Award.

lead: A new report puts a price tag on one of Taylor's surprise performances with Nelly, and the number has fans talking. Almost everything else about that night, from the city to the date, is still missing from the story.

sentences.text: TMZ reports that Taylor paid Nelly $50,000 to join her for a surprise performance.
A News.com.au headline describes it as a three-minute gig.
Neither outlet names a venue or a city.
The report carries no comment from Taylor's team or from Nelly.
Nelly has told a version of this himself: on The Breakfast Club and Good Day New York, he said Taylor called before two Houston shows to explain she was working with a limited budget.
He said her manager, Robert Allen, then handed him $50,000 in a McDonald's bag.
Ashanti joined him in those interviews to talk about their years-long friendship with Taylor.
Coverage of his story still disagrees on when it happened.
His own account and the new report land on the same figure, which is why this one has fans paying attention.

lead: The Bluebird Cafe has a gentle message for anyone planning a Nashville pilgrimage this week: Taylor isn't coming. A viral theory timed to her big Hall of Fame moment ran into a venue calendar with a far simpler explanation.

sentences.text: Taylor was set to join the Nashville Songwriters Hall of Fame on October 26.
A day earlier, a TikToker went viral suggesting she might make a surprise return to the Bluebird.
Fans then spotted a two-day private-event closure on the venue's calendar for October 27 and 28, Country Living notes.
The Bluebird says the closures are for unrelated filming that happens to fall the same week.
It has asked fans not to show up while it is closed.
Cosmopolitan's verdict is that she will not be playing there this week.
The week still delivered its Nashville moment: Brad Paisley inducted her as the hall's youngest member ever, and she spent nearly 10 minutes on Music Row, Liz Rose and being 14.
Her last publicly reported Bluebird set was a surprise appearance in 2018.
